title: Diagnostic Interpretation of Bacterial and Intestinal Cell Free DNA After Perinatal Asphyxia A Critical Translational Review
content: This critical translational review asks whether intestinal epithelial cell-free DNA (cfDNA) adds information at the 48-hour antibiotic reassessment in infants born at or beyond 36 weeks with moderate or severe hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy receiving therapeutic hypothermia. The intended use is interpretation of a reportable bacterial cfDNA signal when conventional findings leave antibiotic continuation uncertain. The searches found no direct validation of the paired plasma measurement in this population. A proposed sample at 36 ± 2 hours allows 10–14 hours for reporting. Prospective evaluation would compare routine findings, bacterial cfDNA and general injury measures with the same model plus intestinal epithelial cfDNA. The primary comparison uses blinded reference adjudication in the prespecified decision population. A stricter reference comparison and sensitivity analyses address shared conventional evidence, unresolved diagnoses and unreportable tests. Added value requires improved classification at acceptable infection sensitivity, adequate calibration and timely results. Intestinal epithelial cfDNA can reflect tissue injury without establishing microbial passage or invasive infection. External validation and a treatment strategy trial are needed before clinical use.
